what.title: What is AAC?
what.lead: AAC — Augmentative and Alternative Communication — is any way of communicating besides talking. For people who are nonspeaking or whose speech is hard to understand, a symbol-and-word app like SayThrough becomes their voice: they tap to build a message, and the device speaks it aloud.
how.title: Three taps to a spoken sentence
how.step1.title: Tap words & symbols
how.step1.body: Choose from color-coded core words and picture symbols, organized for fast access.
how.step2.title: Build the sentence
how.step2.body: Each tap adds to the message bar so you can say a single word or a whole thought.
how.step3.title: Press Speak
how.step3.body: SayThrough reads it aloud in a clear voice — and highlights each word as it's spoken.
who.title: Built with the whole team in mind
who.users.title: AAC users
who.users.body: A dependable voice that works the same everywhere, online or off.
who.families.title: Parents & families
who.families.body: Get started in minutes — free, no account, nothing to buy.
who.teachers.title: Teachers
who.teachers.body: Use it across a classroom of devices — no licences, no logins to manage.
who.slps.title: Speech therapists
who.slps.body: Vocabulary filters, per-profile boards, and consent-based data — free for pros.
features.title: Everything you need to communicate
features.symbols.title: 13,700+ symbols
features.symbols.body: The full open-licensed ARASAAC library, searchable — every word on every board has one, and you can find your own for custom buttons.
features.voice.title: Natural voice, free
features.voice.body: Speaks each sentence aloud and highlights every word as it goes. An optional natural-sounding voice runs entirely on the device — the kind other apps charge for.
features.languages.title: Four languages
features.languages.body: English, Español, Polski and Português — each with its own board built for the language, not machine-translated. Other apps charge per language.
features.offline.title: Works offline
features.offline.body: Install it once; it keeps working with no internet or account.
features.access.title: Every access method
features.access.body: Touch, dwell/hover, and switch scanning — built in.
features.custom.title: Fully customizable
features.custom.body: Edit buttons, add photos, build pages, pick themes and dark mode.
features.profiles.title: Multiple profiles
features.profiles.body: Separate vocabularies and settings per person on one device.
features.noLockIn.title: No lock-in
features.noLockIn.body: Open Board Format import/export moves your boards to or from other apps.
features.grammar.title: Real grammar, not just words
features.grammar.body: Long-press a word for its other forms — plurals and tenses in English, gender agreement in Spanish and Portuguese, all seven cases in Polish.
features.prediction.title: Word prediction
features.prediction.body: Suggests words as you type and learns the ones you actually use — all on your device.
features.sizes.title: Three board sizes
features.sizes.body: From a 26-word starter board to a 513-word expanded one, in every language. Set the level so words appear as they are learned — and never move.
features.backup.title: Full backup
features.backup.body: Save everything — profiles, boards, settings and history — to one file, and restore it on a new device.
features.quick.title: Quick phrases
features.quick.body: One-tap sentences, an attention chime, an emergency phrase, and a history of what was said before.

privacy.title: Private by default
privacy.body: SayThrough is local-first: your profiles, vocabulary, and messages stay on your device. There's no account, and nothing anyone says or types ever leaves the device. The app checks in while it is open so we can see how many people use it. That check-in carries a random code that is thrown away when you close it — not a name, an account, or anything that identifies you — and you can turn it off in Settings.
open.title: Open source
open.body: The code is public, so anyone can verify how it works and how it protects privacy — and the community can help make it better.
cta.title: Ready to give someone a voice?
cta.body: Start talking in your browser right now — free, no sign-up, nothing to install.
contact.lead: SayThrough is a small, free project — messages are read by a person, not a support desk. Here's the fastest route depending on what you need.
contact.broken.title: Something is broken
contact.broken.body: Bug reports are most useful on GitHub, where they can be tracked and fixed in the open: open an issue. If you'd rather not use GitHub, email works too — please say what device and browser you were using.
contact.clinical.title: Vocabulary and clinical feedback
contact.clinical.body: Especially welcome from SLPs, teachers and AAC users. The starter vocabulary is a candidate set awaiting clinical review, so if a word is missing, mis-placed, or the wrong symbol, that feedback directly improves what everyone gets.
contact.else.title: Anything else
contact.else.body: Questions, press, or just telling us how it's going:
contact.noscript: written out to keep it away from scrapers.
contact.privacy.title: Please don't send personal information
contact.privacy.body: Don't include a child's name, diagnosis, school, or anything from inside someone's board. It isn't needed to help, and this is an ordinary email inbox — not a secure or HIPAA-covered channel.

whatIsAac.lead: AAC stands for Augmentative and Alternative Communication — any method of communicating besides speech. It's for people who are nonspeaking, minimally verbal, or whose speech is hard for others to understand.
whatIsAac.vs.title: Augmentative vs. alternative
whatIsAac.vs.body: Augmentative means adding to speech (supporting the words someone already has). Alternative means communicating in place of speech. Many people use a mix, and their needs change over time — AAC meets them wherever they are.
whatIsAac.types.title: Types of AAC
whatIsAac.types.low: No-tech / low-tech: gestures, sign, or paper symbol boards and books.
whatIsAac.types.high: High-tech: apps and devices that speak aloud — like SayThrough — where you tap symbols and words to build messages.
whatIsAac.core.title: What are “core words”?
whatIsAac.core.body: A small set of about 200–400 core words (want, go, more, stop, help, I, you…) makes up roughly 80% of everyday speech. Good AAC keeps these high-frequency words in consistent, easy-to-reach places so they can be found by muscle memory. SayThrough's board is built around core vocabulary, with topic pages for the rest.
whatIsAac.speech.title: Does using AAC stop someone from talking?
whatIsAac.speech.body: No — research consistently shows the opposite. Offering AAC does not prevent speech; for many people it supports language development and can encourage more spoken words, not fewer.
whatIsAac.start.title: How do I get started?
whatIsAac.start.s1: Just start. You don't need a formal evaluation to explore AAC. Open a free app and let the person experience communicating.
whatIsAac.start.s2: Model it. Tap words yourself as you talk (“aided language stimulation”) so they see how messages are built.
whatIsAac.start.s3: Keep it available all the time — not just during “lessons.”
whatIsAac.start.s4: Loop in an SLP (speech-language pathologist) when you can, for personalized goals.
whatIsAac.try: Try it free. SayThrough is a free, open AAC app — no account, works offline. It's a no-cost way to start today.
quickStart.h1: Quick start: your first sentence in 5 minutes
quickStart.lead: No sign-up, no download, nothing to buy. Here's the fastest path from opening SayThrough to hearing it speak.
quickStart.s1.title: 1. Open the app
quickStart.s1.body: Open the app and tap “Try it first — nothing is saved” to jump straight in, or “Let's set up a voice” to create a saved profile (recommended if this is for someone who'll use it regularly). The first thing setup asks is the language — English, Español, Polski or Português. Picking one changes the board, the voice and the app's own words, and you can change it later in Settings.
quickStart.s2.title: 2. Build a message
quickStart.s2.body: You'll see a grid of color-coded words and picture symbols. Tap any word — like I, then want, then more — and each one is added to the message bar at the top.
quickStart.s2.b1: Made a mistake? Tap the ⌫ to remove the last word.
quickStart.s2.b2: Want a different form of a word? Press and hold it (e.g. go → going; in Spanish comer → como, in Polish woda → wodę).
quickStart.s2.b3: Need a word without a button? Open the Keys tab to type it — suggestions appear above the keyboard as you go, and it learns the words you use most.
quickStart.s3.title: 3. Speak it
quickStart.s3.body: Press the green ▶ Speak button and SayThrough reads the whole sentence aloud, highlighting each word as it's spoken. Tapping the sentence itself also speaks it.
quickStart.s3.tip: Tip: In Settings you can turn on “speak each word as you tap,” pick a voice, and adjust the speaking speed.
quickStart.s4.title: 4. Install it on your device
quickStart.s4.body: SayThrough is a web app you can install so it opens full-screen and works offline:
quickStart.s4.ios: iPad / iPhone (Safari): tap the Share icon → Add to Home Screen.
quickStart.s4.chrome: Chromebook / Chrome / Edge: click the Install icon in the address bar (or menu → Install SayThrough).
